trap-negation-contrast.evidence: table( pure-data block, 2 rows. RECOMPUTED at the proton pin: [2]_q = q+1/q = 2.01089686671, so m_e(2+1/[2]_q) = 0.51099895069*2.497290546 = 1.2761128 MeV -> printed 1.2761 CORRECT; (5/2)m_e = 1.2774974 -> printed 1.2775 CORRECT. Percentages against Delta m_p = 1.278 MeV: q-form -0.1477% and classical -0.03933%, printed -0.14% and -0.03% (both truncated rather than rounded; rounding would give -0.15% and -0.04%). PIN DISCRIMINATION: at this precision the table cannot separate ANY of the three candidate pins -- proton, muon and even the erroneous 1.1097 all give 1.2761 MeV, because 1/[2]_q is stationary to first order near q=1.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: FINDING (the block's own table refutes its parent). prop:partition-sum-proton-residual states of the boxed q-deformed identity Delta m_p = m_e(2 + 1/[2]_q): 'This matches the observed proton residual to within 0.1%.' The recomputed agreement is 0.1477%, and THIS TABLE'S OWN FIRST ROW PRINTS -0.14%. The parent's 'within 0.1%' is true only of the CLASSICAL q->1 form (0.039%), which is the row the boxed equation does not assert. Proposed fix: change the parent's claim to 'to within 0.15%', or state the two forms separately as the table already does.
